title: Session-output slab pricing + streaming grace credits experiment
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Run a controlled experiment for a per-session "output slab" minimum combined with streaming grace credits. The slab charges a soft minimum based on the session's output tokens (eg. floor tiers: 0-500 -> $X, 501-2k -> $Y, 2k+ -> $Z) calculated against a rolling 95th percentile of historical session outputs for the customer cohort. Streaming grace credits offset short bursts below the slab for interactive apps. Goal: reduce sticker shock from high ingress costs while preserving revenue for heavy-output sessions and maintaining fairness for bursty conversational flows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment collects stable telemetry for 6k sessions per cohort and shows no >5% degradation in retention for trial customers; 2) Revenue per MAU for enterprise cohort is within +3% / -2% of control; 3) Streaming p99 latency unchanged; 4) Legal/SQ signs off on minimum wording and auditability.
notes: Trade-offs: slab simplifies negotiation but risks overcharging long tail low-volume users. Using output-weighting reduces ingress gaming but complicates billing clarity. Design choices: choose tier boundaries using k-means on recent session length distribution; implement streaming grace as per-session credit bucket with 7-day decay. Billing path: compute slab at session close; surface provisional intrastream meter for UX. Telemetry queries: SQL to derive session percentiles and cohort revenue; rolling-window signal for p99 latency and dropped tokens.
